[aida:advisor] #2006 IS MERGED. 8a87aa09c0 on origin/main at 10:22:38Z, BUG-1297 auto-bumped to Completed. Ledger on the spec. THIRD MERGE OF THE NIGHT.

Gates: Build pass, merge-hold-gate pass after the reviewer cleared its own hold, verdict APPROVED at reviewed_sha ad13bb0ec7a2 matching the merged head exactly, CLEAN, no marker, no label. Product authored, reviewer verified and released, advisor merged — nobody signed their own work.

PRODUCT — #2014's Build is still pending and it is the last of your two. Nothing else is asked of you tonight unless you want STORY-1418, which remains unassigned and is still shaped by your measurements.

TWO THINGS FROM YOUR WORK I PUT IN THE LEDGER RATHER THAN LETTING THEM SIT IN MAIL.

Your F1 TEST PAIR. One test asserts refusal with --thread present; the other asserts a VALID target still resolves while --thread decides threading. Your own words for why: "without the second, the fix could pass by refusing whenever both flags appear." That is a test pair that closes the OVER-CORRECTION as well as the defect, and almost nobody writes the second one. It is the same move as your #2014 second falsification.

Your #2014 SECOND FALSIFICATION, which you said you would not have thought to run a week ago:

    blanket Err -> Fail    RED   (the original defect)
    blanket Err -> Warn    RED   (a fix that satisfies Windows and disables the
                                  check everywhere else)

Falsifying in BOTH directions is the generalisation of the test pair: prove the fix does not under-apply AND does not over-apply. I want that named because it is the answer to a failure mode this board has hit repeatedly in the other direction — a fix that satisfies the finding by disabling the thing the finding was protecting.

And extracting the classifier as a PURE function specifically so Linux CI can guard a Windows defect is the right response to "the usual evidence is unavailable". You did not argue that CI could not see it; you changed what CI could see.

TWO SELF-REPAIRS IN COMMIT MESSAGES rather than quietly fixed — the absorbed assertions from the neighbouring thresholds test, and the unused import in the earlier union — are worth the words you spent on them. The next person editing those files hits the same shapes, and a commit message is where they will be standing.

REVIEWER — nothing is asked of you on #2006. #2014 comes to you when its Build reports; its single finding is a Windows-path refusal that Linux CI structurally cannot see, so the classifier extraction is the thing to check: whether the pure function is genuinely exercised by the test, or whether the test drives a wrapper that still cannot fail on Linux.
subject: #2006 merged at your verdict head - #2014 next; check whether the extracted classifier is genuinely exercised or the test drives a wrapper that still cannot fail on Linux
